t: Except as provided in section 44945 of title 49, United States Code, funds appropriated or transferred to Transportation Security Administration “Aviation Security”, “Administration” and “Transportation Security Support” for fiscal years 2004, 2005, 2006, and 2007 that are recovered or deobligated shall be available only for the procurement or installation of explosives detection systems, for air cargo, baggage, and checkpoint screening systems, subject to notification: Provided, That quarterly reports shall be submitted to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives on any funds that are recovered or deobligated.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "subject to notification" and the quarterly reports amount to consultation before a federal decision. Those notifications and reports go only to the congressional Appropriations Committees, which are inside the federal government. The section otherwise just restricts how recovered or deobligated TSA funds may be used, and no state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public is involved.
fable.s: quarterly reports shall be submitted to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives on any funds that are recovered or deobligated

qwen_block.w: The section requires the submission of reports to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. The mention of 'notification' is vague but does not specify an outside party, and the primary procedural requirement is the report to Congress.
qwen_block.s: quarterly reports shall be submitted to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives on any funds that are recovered or deobligated.

opus.w: This section limits how recovered or deobligated TSA funds may be spent and requires notification and quarterly reports to the congressional Appropriations Committees. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so these reports and notices are not participation. No state, company, expert, or member of the public is consulted, and the section creates no right to sue.
opus.s: quarterly reports shall be submitted to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives on any funds that are recovered or deobligated

qwen_chat.w: The section requires reports to be submitted to congressional committees. Congress is inside the federal government, so reporting to it does not constitute participation with an outside party. The mention of 'notification' in the main clause is a condition for fund usage, not a requirement for public consultation or input.
qwen_chat.s: Provided, That quarterly reports shall be submitted to the Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives on any funds that are recovered or deobligated.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "notification" implies some form of participation or consultation with an outside party. However, the text specifies that reports are submitted to the "Committees on Appropriations of the Senate and the House of Representatives." Congress is part of the federal government (inside the boundary), so reporting to it is not participation with an outside party. Furthermore, the "notification" mentioned in the main clause is a condition for the use of funds, not a procedural requirement for public input or consultation before a decision is made.
